name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; England low impact
summary: US flu admissions rose 38% to 8,396 in the week to 31 Oct; England's flu admissions rising but in the low-impact range
state: US hospitals logged 8,396 flu admissions in the week to 31 Oct, up 38% on the week before, with the CDC describing activity as higher than usual for the time of year and forecasting further rises to 21 Nov (Medical Daily, 9 Nov). UKHSA reported on 12 Nov that flu admissions in England rose to 3.65 per 100,000 in the week to 8 Nov, still in the low-impact range, with COVID-19 stable at baseline. An unusually early US season meets Watch; no health systems are reported as strained.
for_you: Those eligible for a free NHS flu or COVID-19 vaccine can book through the NHS. UKHSA advises staying at home when unwell with a high temperature where possible.
rubric_hit: Watch: a hemisphere's flu season unusually early (US admissions 8,396 in week to 31 Oct, above usual for the time of year)

sources.title: Medical Daily — Flu hospital admissions rose 38% to 8,396 in one week

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
